deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). X is a projective plane carrying an arrangement of (pseudo-)lines Δ_α. X^∨ is the dual plane, Σ is the dual configuration, and the incidence/flag space 𝔛 has natural maps to X and to X^∨. Under duality:
- a point δ of X corresponds to a line D_δ of X^∨;
- a line Δ_α corresponds to a point s_α ∈ Σ;
- an edge a_α ⊂ Δ_α of the arrangement corresponds to the pencil of lines through s_α;
- a vertex a_α ∩ a_β corresponds to the line through s_α and s_β.

The previous page says that orientations of a face F correspond to orientations of the line D. Moving δ continuously inside F corresponds to moving D continuously. The page then sets out to read the polygonal structure of F (its circuit of edges and vertices) in dual terms.

The construction on this page:
1. Start at δ_0 ∈ F, so D = D_0 = D_{δ_0}, with the orientation ω_D induced by ω_F. Move δ in a straight line to a point δ_1 on (near) the edge a_α. In the dual, D sweeps in the direction given by the orientation until D_1 passes through s_α.
2. Travel along a_α in the direction induced by the orientation of F. Dually, D_1 pivots around s_α. The direction of pivoting must be made explicit. It is fixed by the orientation of D_1, transported from D_0, together with the pseudo-geometric configuration.
3. Orientation bookkeeping. On the X side, three data form a compatible system: the orientation ω_α of Δ_α carrying a_α, the orientation ω_{δ_1} of the points δ_1 on a_α, and the 'rose' (circle of directions) ρ_α of Δ_α at the point. On the dual side, at the contact flag (s_α, D_1), the corresponding data form an ANTI-compatible system: ω ∈ ω(X, s_α), ω_{D_1}, and ρ'_α, the rotation sense of the sweep ('balayage'). In other words, the orientation of D_1 is the inverse of the one induced by ω on the sweep. This sign rule lets one propagate orientations along the circuit.
4. D_1 keeps pivoting until it first hits another point s_β of Σ. This is exactly the moment δ reaches the vertex δ_2 = a_α ∩ a_β = Δ_α ∩ Δ_β. The pivot then switches to s_β, and one continues in the same way.
5. Caveat in square brackets: during the sweep, D can also pass through specialisations, i.e. lines through vertices s_β that are not reached as pivots. Those do not count as vertices of F.

What this achieves. The boundary circuit of a face F of a line arrangement is identified with a 'windmill' or gift-wrapping process in the dual. A line rotates about a point of Σ until it hits another point of Σ, then rotates about that new point, and so on. Orientations are tracked through the non-orientable projective plane by explicit compatible/anticompatible sign rules at contact flags. The next page analyses 'half-circuits' around points of order 0, 1, 2. All of this serves Grothendieck's project of a topological or combinatorial duality theory for systems of pseudo-lines.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The direction of pivoting is explicitly left open ('dans un sens qu'il faudra expliciter').
The compatible/anticompatible sign claim is asserted by reference to a figure, not proved.

The bracketed remark on spurious specialisations (lines through points of Σ that are swept past but are not pivots) is only half-formulated. It needs care in the pseudo-line setting, where 'straight-line motion' of δ inside F has no a priori meaning unless F is given some pseudo-convex structure.

ideas.what: Point/line duality: faces, edges and vertices of a line arrangement correspond to line-partitions of the dual point set, pencils through s_α, and lines through two points of Σ.
ideas.modern_name: projective duality between line arrangements and point configurations (cells ↔ combinatorial types of line-partitions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in combinatorial form Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Edelsbrunner

ideas.what: The boundary circuit of a face, read dually as a line pivoting successively around points of Σ ('balayage').
ideas.modern_name: rotating sweep / windmill process / gift wrapping; related to allowable sequences

ideas.what: Orientation transport through a non-orientable projective plane: correspondence between orientations of a face F and orientations of the dual line D, with compatible vs anticompatible sign rules at contact flags (s, D).
ideas.modern_name: orientation bookkeeping in the flag/incidence space of a (topological) projective plane; local orientation conventions in oriented-matroid-style duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific source known for this exact formulation

ideas.what: Spurious specialisations (lines through points of Σ that are swept past but are not vertices of the face).
ideas.modern_name: degenerate events in a rotational sweep

missed.claim: A sign rule (compatible on the X side, anticompatible on the dual flag side) for propagating orientations along face circuits under pseudo-line duality, with the pivoting direction left to be made explicit.
missed.quote: forment un système anticompatible, i.e. l'orientation ω_{D_1} de D, est inverse
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Orientation conventions are central in topological duality for pseudoline arrangements (Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu). An independent, orientation-explicit treatment of 1983–84 would be of historical interest. It is probably not new mathematics.

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out, essentially independently and at the same time as Goodman–Pollack, the dual 'sweep' picture of arrangement cells within his pseudo-line programme.
missed.quote: D_1 continue ... jusqu'à un moment où il rencontre un premier sommet (qui sera s_β)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's engagement with combinatorial geometry topics later formalised in oriented matroid theory. Mathematically it is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the classical windmill/rotating-sweep dual description of a face boundary, plus careful orientation bookkeeping. It is a natural and correct working-out step, but it is known in the combinatorial geometry literature, apart from the specific anticompatibility formulation.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'D = D_0 = D_β' should likely read 'D = D_0 = D_{δ_0}' (or D_δ), consistent with the previous page.
'le rôle ρ_α' and 'ρ'_α = rôle de basculage' are uncertain; the word may be 'rose', i.e. the circle of directions ('rose ... du balayage'). Uncertain.
'la vie pseudo-géométrique' is probably 'la vue' or similar; uncertain.
'compatible au sens des flèches' may instead read 'au sens de Stokes' or similar; uncertain.
Last left-column line: likely 'de propager le long de a_α [l'orientation] ... toujours'.
